body:
lena: Quick flag from signal team: cost attribution gaps keep showing up for traces sampled before enrichment. We get uncharged spans in analytics.

otis: Is this the path where the edge proxy emits minimal spans and enrichment happens async?

lena: Yep. Sampler runs early, enrichment attaches tenant_id / billing_id later. If sampler drops, we literally have no link.

anika: Two patterns to consider: 1) push enrichment earlier (adds latency to edge), 2) piggyback a tiny proof on the span so sampler can decide with billing context.

mo: Another option: deterministic tenant-preserve list. Keep 100% for paying-tenants, probabilistic for others. But identifying paying-tenants upstream is messy.

lena: I like piggybacking but worried about leaking billing_id everywhere.

anika: What about HMACing the billing_id with a proxy-only salt and including tag header? Sampler checks tag; enrichment can fetch raw key from secure store. Tag is non-reversible without salt.

otis: That avoids a transient KV, fewer writes. But need to manage salt rotation and ensure proxies use the same salt regionally.

sec-bot: reminder: any scheme including derived billing tokens must be reviewed under security policy S-4 (ephemeral secrets).

mo: If HMAC fails (legacy clients or missing header) fall back to a beacon write: span_id -> encrypted-billing (TTL 8s). This only happens for <1% of traffic.

anika: For KV approach we should namespace by region + minute bucket to allow efficient eviction. Also limit max entries per-tenant to protect Redis.

lena: Perf note: measured in staging — adding HMAC header ~+60 bytes per request, no measurable p50 change. Beacon write path added ~1ms p95 at 10k rps.

otis: Operational costs: if we wrote beacons for 0.5% of 2M rps peak -> 10k writes/s sustained => plan for a small write-optimized Redis ring or Dynamo with TTLs. Estimate ~$2000/mo for modest cluster.

anika: Security workflow: encrypt payload with service key, store only ciphertext, use KMS for decryption in enrich path, auto-delete after TTL. Also log-only masked billing_id when we detect misses.

mo: Edge case: retries can create duplicate beacon writes. Use idempotent setex by span_id; duplicates are cheap.

lena: Monitoring: beacon_write_rate, beacon_hit_rate, enrich_stitch_latency, missed_billing_count. Add alert if missed_billing_count > 0.01% of ingested traces for 5m.

anika: Sampling policy change: keep any trace with valid HMAC tag OR beacon present. Otherwise sample probabilistically. We should preserve a higher debug-sample for low-volume tenants.

otis: Implementation plan: phase 1 HMAC-only on canary proxies for 48h -> collect sightlines (anika + otis). Phase 2 deploy beacon fallback if misses exceed threshold (mo + infra). Phase 3 security review + key rotation (sec team).

deploy-bot: canary-proxy v1.4 -> promoted to canary cluster (eu-west-1) :rocket:

sec-bot: created task SEC-1122 for key-management review, assigned to sec-ops.

lena: Action items captured: - anika/otis: run HMAC canary & dashboard - mo/infra: prototype beacon fallback (TTL 8s, encrypted) - sec-ops: KMS/key rotation review - platform: add metrics + alerting.

anika: I'll produce a short RFC with perf numbers and tradeoffs, call it "HMAC-first sampling + beacon fallback" and link to the spike.

otis: Timeline: canary metrics in 48h -> decision by EOD Fri.

mo: One more thought: add a circuit-breaker on beacon writes per-tenant to avoid hot-tenant storms consuming KV capacity.

lena: Good call. We'll cap at 500 writes/s per-tenant and emit a 'beacon-rate-limited' metric.

anika: Ok closing the loop here, I'll drop the RFC link in #rfc once ready. Thanks everyone. :+1:
